chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Khalid ibn Madd al-Qalanisi, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever completes the Quran at Makkah from one Friday to another Friday, or less than that, or more, and completes it on a Friday, Allah will record for him the reward and the good deeds from the first Friday that ever was in the world to the last Friday that will ever be; and if he completes it on any other day, likewise.

key_terms.الْأَجْرُ وَالْحَسَنَات: Reward and good deeds/merits recorded in the divine ledger of the afterlife
key_terms.خَتَمَ الْقُرْآنَ: Completing the full recitation of the Quran (khatm al-Quran), a spiritually meritorious act
key_terms.مَكَّة: Makkah, the holiest city in Islam and site of the Masjid al-Haram and the Ka'bah
key_terms.يَوْمُ جُمُعَة: Friday, the blessed weekly holy day in Islam

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for completing the Quran recitation at Makkah on a Friday?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) describes an extraordinary merit of completing a full recitation of the Quran (khatm) at Makkah. The hadith specifies that if the completion falls on a Friday, God records for that person the accumulated reward of every Friday from the beginning of the world to its end. If completed on another day, an equivalent reward is granted. This reflects the special sanctity of Makkah and the blessing of Friday in Islamic tradition, encouraging pilgrims and residents to complete Quran recitations there.
